hints: On a velocity-time graph, displacement is represented by the signed area between the graph and the time axis.
From $t = 0$ to $t = 10$, the velocity is negative, forming an inverted trapezium with parallel sides of lengths 10 and 4, and height 6.
walkthrough:
Displacement is the signed area under the velocity-time graph. For $P$ between $t = 0$ and $t = 10$, the region lies below the time axis as a trapezium of parallel sides $10$ and $4$, and depth $6$:
$$s(10) = -\frac{1}{2}(10 + 4) \times 6 = -\frac{1}{2}(14) \times 6 = -7 \times 6 = -42\text{ m}$$
teacher_walkthrough: Recall that displacement is the net signed area bounded by the velocity-time graph and the time axis.
Identify the geometric shape between $t = 0$ and $t = 10$: it is a trapezium located below the time axis with parallel horizontal lengths $10$ and $4$, and vertical height $6$.

Apply the area formula for a trapezium and assign a negative sign because the velocity is negative:
$$s = -\frac{a + b}{2} \times h = -\frac{10 + 4}{2} \times 6 = -7 \times 6 = -42\text{ m}$$

hints: The line segment passing through $t = 10$ with $v = 0$ is a straight line that connects $(6, -6)$ to $(10, 0)$.
Find the gradient of this straight line segment: $m = \frac{0 - (-6)}{10 - 6} = \frac{6}{4} = 1.5\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
walkthrough:
Determine the constant gradient of the straight line segment from $(6, -6)$ to $(10, 0)$:
$$\text{gradient} = \frac{0 - (-6)}{10 - 6} = \frac{6}{4} = 1.5\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Since the segment continues with the same gradient up to $t = 12\text{ s}$, calculate $v(12)$:
$$v(12) = v(10) + \text{gradient} \times (12 - 10) = 0 + 1.5(2) = 3\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
teacher_walkthrough: Identify the line segment on the graph passing through $t = 10$: it connects $(6, -6)$ to $(10, 0)$ and continues straight past $t = 10$.

Calculate the slope (acceleration) of this line segment:
$$a = \frac{\Delta v}{\Delta t} = \frac{0 - (-6)}{10 - 6} = \frac{6}{4} = 1.5\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Apply the linear equation from $t = 10\text{ s}$ where $v = 0\text{ m s}^{-1}$ to $t = 12\text{ s}$:
$$v = u + at = 0 + 1.5 \times (12 - 10) = 1.5 \times 2 = 3\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

ai_rubric.Interpreting Motion Graphs: Finds gradient $\frac{6}{4} = 1.5$ and computes $v(12) = 1.5 \times 2 = 3\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

hints: Total distance is the sum of the positive areas of both regions.
The first region ($0 \le t \le 10$) has area $42\text{ m}$.
The second region ($10 \le t \le T$) is a triangle with base $(T - 10)$ and peak height $v = 3\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
walkthrough:
Total distance is the sum of the absolute areas of the two parts of the velocity-time graph for $P$:
$$\text{Distance} = \text{Area}_1 + \text{Area}_2 = 42 + \text{Area}_2$$

The region for $10 \le t \le T$ is a triangle with base $(T - 10)$ and height $v = 3\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$\text{Area}_2 = \frac{1}{2}(T - 10) \times 3 = 1.5(T - 10)$$

Set the total distance equal to $49.5\text{ m}$ and solve for $T$:
$$42 + 1.5(T - 10) = 49.5$$
$$1.5(T - 10) = 7.5 \implies T - 10 = \frac{7.5}{1.5} = 5$$
$$T = 10 + 5 = 15\text{ s}$$
teacher_walkthrough: Recall that distance travelled is the sum of the geometric areas regardless of whether velocity is positive or negative.

The distance travelled in the first phase ($0 \le t \le 10$) is the magnitude of the displacement from part (i):
$$d_1 = 42\text{ m}$$

The remaining distance covered in the positive direction ($10 \le t \le T$) must be:
$$d_2 = 49.5 - 42 = 7.5\text{ m}$$

This second phase forms a triangle with base $(T - 10)$ and maximum height $v = 3\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$\frac{1}{2} \times (T - 10) \times 3 = 7.5$$
$$1.5(T - 10) = 7.5$$

Divide both sides by $1.5$:
$$T - 10 = 5 \implies T = 15\text{ s}$$

ai_rubric.Interpreting Motion Graphs: Sets up $42 + \frac{1}{2}(T - 10) \times 3 = 49.5$ and solves for $T = 15\text{ s}$.

hints: Particle $Q$ starts from rest at $t = 2$ and accelerates uniformly at $1.75\text{ m s}^{-2}$ until $t = 6$: $V = u + at = 0 + 1.75(6 - 2) = 7\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

Find the displacement of $Q$ at $t = 15$: $Q$'s graph is a trapezium with base $(15 - 2) = 13$, top parallel side $(12 - 6) = 6$, and height $V = 7$: $\text{Displacement}_Q = \frac{1}{2}(13 + 6) \times 7 = 66.5\text{ m}$.
Find the final displacement of $P$: $s_P = -42 + 7.5 = -34.5\text{ m}$.
The distance between the particles is $|s_Q - s_P| = 66.5 - (-34.5) = 101\text{ m}$.
walkthrough:
Calculate the peak velocity $V$ of particle $Q$ using $v = u + at$ with $u = 0$, $a = 1.75\text{ m s}^{-2}$, and $\Delta t = 6 - 2 = 4\text{ s}$:
$$V = 0 + 1.75(4) = 7\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

Calculate the displacement of particle $Q$ between $t = 2$ and $t = T = 15$. The graph for $Q$ is a trapezium with parallel sides of lengths $15 - 2 = 13$ and $12 - 6 = 6$, and height $V = 7$:
$$s_Q = \frac{1}{2}(13 + 6) \times 7 = \frac{1}{2}(19) \times 7 = 9.5 \times 7 = 66.5\text{ m}$$

Calculate the final displacement of particle $P$ from the origin $O$ at $t = 15$:
$$s_P = -42 + 7.5 = -34.5\text{ m}$$

Calculate the distance between particles $P$ and $Q$ at $t = 15$:
$$\text{Distance} = s_Q - s_P = 66.5 - (-34.5) = 66.5 + 34.5 = 101\text{ m}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Determine the maximum speed $V$ reached by $Q$ during its initial acceleration from $t = 2\text{ s}$ to $t = 6\text{ s}$:
$$V = u + a\Delta t = 0 + 1.75 \times (6 - 2) = 1.75 \times 4 = 7\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

Compute the displacement of particle $Q$ by finding the area of its trapezium from $t = 2$ to $t = 15$:
- Bottom base on time axis: $15 - 2 = 13\text{ s}$
- Top parallel horizontal section: $12 - 6 = 6\text{ s}$
- Height: $V = 7\text{ m s}^{-1}$

Apply the trapezium formula:
$$s_Q = \frac{a + b}{2} \times h = \frac{13 + 6}{2} \times 7 = \frac{19}{2} \times 7 = 9.5 \times 7 = 66.5\text{ m}$$

Determine the position of particle $P$ at $t = 15\text{ s}$ relative to origin $O$:
- Initial displacement up to $t = 10$: $-42\text{ m}$
- Subsequent positive displacement from $t = 10$ to $t = 15$: $+7.5\text{ m}$
$$s_P = -42 + 7.5 = -34.5\text{ m}$$

Calculate the separation distance between the two particles:
$$\text{Distance} = s_Q - s_P = 66.5 - (-34.5) = 66.5 + 34.5 = 101\text{ m}$$

ai_rubric.Interpreting Motion Graphs: Finds $V = 1.75 \times 4 = 7\text{ m s}^{-1}$, calculates $s_Q = 66.5\text{ m}$ and $s_P = -34.5\text{ m}$, giving separation distance $66.5 - (-34.5) = 101\text{ m}$.
